enum.audio.aac.10: Apple's lossless codec, used by Apple Music and iTunes.
enum.audio.aac.11: Completely uncompressed and the largest; for post-production and professional audio.
enum.audio.aac.12: Keeps the original audio track untouched — very fast with zero quality loss.
enum.audio.aac.13: Removes the audio track, keeping only the picture.
enum.audio.aac.6: The standard audio codec for MP4/M4A. Best compatibility, better than MP3 at the same bitrate.
enum.audio.aac.7: The most compatible audio format. Every device plays it; less efficient than AAC.
enum.audio.aac.8: A modern open codec with the best quality per bit. Great for speech and streaming.
enum.audio.aac.9: Lossless compression, about 60% the size of WAV with the audio fully preserved.
enum.codec.h264.10: The newest open codec with the highest compression (about 50% smaller than H.264), but much slower to encode. Good for archiving.
enum.codec.h264.11: Apple's intermediate editing format: nearly lossless but very large (about 10× H.264). For Final Cut / Premiere workflows, not for distribution.
enum.codec.h264.12: 256-colour animation without sound. Extremely compatible but inefficient; suits short loops.
enum.codec.h264.2: Smaller files at the same quality
enum.codec.h264.7: The most compatible codec — every device, browser and editor opens it. Medium size at equal quality, and the fastest to encode.
enum.codec.h264.8: H.265: about 30–50% smaller than H.264 at the same quality, but older devices and some web players may not support it.
enum.codec.h264.9: Google's open codec and the standard choice for WebM. Royalty-free playback on the web. Better compression than H.264, slower to encode.
enum.hash.md5: 128-bit; most commonly used to check whether a file was modified
enum.hash.md5.3: 256-bit; the modern standard for verification and signing
enum.hash.md5.5: 32-bit cyclic redundancy check for detecting transfer errors
